summary: Gov. Greg Abbott (Republican) ran again but lost to Gina Hinojosa (Democrat), and he conceded.

candidates.name: Gina Hinojosa
candidates.bio: Gina Hinojosa is a member of the Texas House of Representatives from Austin, serving since 2017. She was the Democratic nominee for governor in 2026.

positions.summary: Proposes a one-time $1,500 refund for every Texas household, paid from the Rainy Day Fund, and a freeze on home electricity rates until data centers and other large users pay their own costs.
Criticizes Abbott's border spending, saying billions went to prosecuting immigrants for trespassing and paying for their legal defense.
Says she would end the voucher program and the STAAR test and fire Education Commissioner Mike Morath on her first day.

candidates.name: Greg Abbott
candidates.bio: Greg Abbott is the governor of Texas, in office since 2015. He previously served as state attorney general from 2002 to 2015 and as a Texas Supreme Court justice.

positions.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment letting voters eliminate school district property taxes on homesteads and lowering the homestead appraisal cap from 10% to 3%.
Proposes capping monthly co-pays for inhalers and epinephrine at $25 and creating a lower-cost Essential Benefits Health Insurance Plan.
Says illegal immigrants arrested for violent felonies must be denied bail and proposes expanding the DPS repeat offender task force.
Proposes Student Success Academies for struggling readers and math students, limits on classroom devices, and a requirement that 70% of funding go to classrooms.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called); also confirmed by wcax.com report Summary originally noted that percentages came from Wikipedia and might update, and that election-night partial counts differed.
